title: Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 1.II: Pelagius refuses the grace that heals and turns the will by infusing faith and charity — leaves the will in indifference
pass_a_gloss: II. Now, in the second place let us see what he willed not to admit. Briefly I say: Pelagius willed not that grace of God which by its efficacy would heal the will, and change it from evil unto good, by infusing into it faith, charity, and the rest which bring with them spiritual life and everlasting salvation: but he admitted only that (as has been said) which illuminates the mind, moves the affections, invites the will; yet so that it leaves the will to itself, and does not move it from the balance of its indifference, waiting namely from the will itself for the act of believing, of converting, and the like, not working these acts in it.
pass_b_english: II. Second: what he would not admit. Briefly: Pelagius refused the grace that by its efficacy heals the will and turns it from evil to good by pouring in faith, charity, and the rest that bring spiritual life and everlasting salvation. He admitted only what lights the mind, moves the affections, and invites the will—yet so as to leave the will to itself and not shift it from indifference’s balance, waiting on the will for the act of believing, converting, and the like, not working those acts in it.
source_text: II. Jam, secundo in loco videamus qualem noluit admittere. Breviter dico: Illam gratiam Dei noluit Pelagius, quae sua efficacitate sanaret voluntatem, et ex mala in bonam commutaret, infundendo illi fidem, charitatem, reliquaque quae vitam spiritualem et salutem aeternam secum apportant: sed admisit eam solummodo (ut dictum est) quae illuminat mentem, movet affectus, invitat voluntatem; ita tamen ut eam permittat sibi, et ab aequilibrio indifferentiae suae non dimoveat, exspectans scilicet ab ipsa voluntate actum credendi, convertendi, ac consimilia, non operans in ipsa hosce actus.
